quests.instruction: A ripe mango and a fresh pomelo both share this zesty, lively flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a flavor that's fun and bright, not plain and mild.
quests.explanation: Nice work! A ripe mango and fresh pomelo both share this zesty, lively flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: A tangy flavor is a sharp, strong taste that wakes up your mouth.

quests.instruction: Cranberries and green apples both have a pleasantly sharp flavor, not as strong as a lemon's. What word fits?
quests.hint: This taste is a gentler cousin of a very sour flavor, still a little sharp but pleasant.
quests.explanation: You found it! Cranberries and green apples both have this pleasantly sharp flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Tart foods make your mouth pucker up because they are so sour.

quests.instruction: An overripe banana perfect for baking bread and a soft, overripe plum share this squishy texture. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This word describes the texture of fruit that's begun to break down.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! An overripe banana perfect for baking and a soft, overripe plum share this squishy texture, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Mushy fruit has become extremely soft and easy to squash.

quests.instruction: An overripe kiwi and a very soft, overripe tomato both feel squishy rather than firm. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This word describes fruit that's gone soft past the point of a satisfying crunch.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! An overripe kiwi and very soft, overripe tomato both feel squishy rather than firm, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Overripe bananas get mushy and are perfect for baking bread.

quests.instruction: A ripe mango and a fresh nectarine both drip with liquid the moment you slice them. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit that's far from dry inside.
quests.explanation: Terrific! A ripe mango and fresh nectarine both drip with liquid when sliced, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Juicy fruits are filled with water and incredibly refreshing to eat.

quests.instruction: A ripe passion fruit and a fresh guava share this bright, zesty flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This word describes a flavor with a fun, zesty edge to its sweetness.
quests.explanation: Yes! A ripe passion fruit and fresh guava share this bright, zesty flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Many citrus fruits have a wonderfully tangy kick.

quests.instruction: A very ripe banana and an overripe pear both feel soft enough to mash with just a fork. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes the texture of fruit well past its crunchy stage.
quests.explanation: That's right! A very ripe banana and overripe pear both feel soft enough to mash with a fork, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Mushy fruit is very easy for babies to eat.

quests.instruction: A ripe cantaloupe wedge and a watermelon slice both practically drip down your arm. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit best eaten with a napkin close by.
quests.explanation: Great job! A ripe cantaloupe wedge and watermelon slice both practically drip, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Watermelons and oranges are famously juicy.

quests.instruction: A watermelon slice and a ripe cherry share this same sugary flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This is the taste balanced out by its tangy or tart opposite in many recipes.
quests.explanation: You got it! A watermelon slice and ripe cherry share this sugary flavor, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Sweetness in fruit comes from natural sugars.

quests.instruction: A ripe kiwi and a fresh mandarin both have a bright, zippy flavor mixed with their sweetness. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste sits between fully sweet and fully sour, with a lively zip.
quests.explanation: Well done! A ripe kiwi and fresh mandarin both have this bright, zippy flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Tangy flavors make your tongue tingle.

quests.instruction: A lime wedge and a fresh currant share this tangy, puckering taste. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This taste is the opposite of the flavor in a ripe, juicy mango.
quests.explanation: Correct! A lime wedge and fresh currant share this tangy, puckering taste called sour!
quests.funFact: Sour fruits have a high level of acidity that makes your mouth pucker.

quests.instruction: A crisp apple and a firm, unripe pear both make a loud snap with every bite. Which word describes that?
quests.hint: This word describes the sound and feel of a fruit that snaps, not squishes.
quests.explanation: Super! A crisp apple and a firm, unripe pear both make a loud snap with every bite, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Crunchy fruits make a loud snapping sound when you bite into them.

quests.instruction: A ripe pineapple and a fresh fig both share this sugary flavor. Which word describes it?
quests.hint: This is the taste that makes fruit feel like a natural treat.
quests.explanation: Nice work! A ripe pineapple and fresh fig both share this sugary flavor, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Our bodies naturally crave sweet fruits because they provide quick energy.

quests.instruction: A fresh lemon and a lime both make your mouth pucker the same way. Which taste word fits both?
quests.hint: This taste can make your eyes squint a little.
quests.explanation: You found it! A fresh lemon and lime both share that mouth-puckering taste called sour!
quests.funFact: Lemons and limes are the most famous sour fruits.

quests.instruction: A firm jicama and a fresh water chestnut share this same snappy bite. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a texture with a satisfying snap, not a soft squish.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! A firm jicama and fresh water chestnut share this same snappy bite, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: A fresh apple is famously crunchy and crisp.

quests.instruction: A crisp Granny Smith apple and a spoonful of cranberry sauce share this same bright flavor. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a sharp taste that still feels pleasant, not overwhelming.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! A crisp Granny Smith apple and cranberry sauce share this same bright flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Cranberries are famous for being incredibly tart.

quests.instruction: An unripe persimmon can leave a strange, sharp feeling in your mouth, a taste called ___. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste can make your whole mouth feel oddly dry and sharp at once.
quests.explanation: Terrific! The strange, sharp feeling an unripe persimmon leaves in your mouth is called bitter!
quests.funFact: Bitter is a sharp taste that many people have to learn to like.

quests.instruction: A ripe orange segment and a slice of pineapple both drip with sweet liquid. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a texture, not a specific taste like sweet or sour.
quests.explanation: Yes! A ripe orange segment and slice of pineapple both drip with sweet liquid, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: A really juicy fruit will drip down your chin when you bite it.

quests.instruction: A slice of rhubarb pie and a spoonful of cranberry sauce both share this bright flavor. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This taste is milder than sour, but still brighter than plain sweet.
quests.explanation: That's right! Rhubarb pie and cranberry sauce both share this bright flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Bakers often add lots of sugar to tart fruits to make them taste better.

quests.instruction: A fresh, firm apple slice and an unripe pear slice both share this same crisp bite. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes the sound a fresh fruit makes, not a squishy one.
quests.explanation: Great job! A fresh, firm apple slice and unripe pear slice both share this same crisp bite, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Crunchy fruits are great for your teeth and jaw muscles.

quests.instruction: A very ripe avocado and an overripe peach both feel soft enough to squish with just a light touch. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes texture, not taste, once a fruit is past its firmest stage.
quests.explanation: You got it! A very ripe avocado and overripe peach both feel soft enough to squish, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: You can easily mash mushy fruit with just a fork.

quests.instruction: A tart gooseberry and an unripe peach share this same sharp bite. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste often fades the longer a fruit ripens in the sun.
quests.explanation: Well done! A tart gooseberry and unripe peach share this same sharp bite called sour!
quests.funFact: Adding sugar to sour lemon juice makes delicious lemonade.

quests.instruction: An unripe mango and a quince eaten straight off the tree share this sharp taste. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste often disappears the longer a fruit is left to ripen.
quests.explanation: Correct! An unripe mango and a quince eaten straight off the tree share this sharp taste, called bitter!
quests.funFact: The white part of an orange peel is extremely bitter.

quests.instruction: A ripe star fruit and a fresh papaya share this bright, zippy flavor. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a flavor that's exciting without being too sharp.
quests.explanation: Super! A ripe star fruit and fresh papaya share this bright, zippy flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Yogurt often has a slightly tangy taste from healthy bacteria.

quests.instruction: A very overripe pear and an overripe tomato both feel soft and squishy to the touch. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes fruit texture that has gone past crisp and firm.
quests.explanation: Nice work! A very overripe pear and overripe tomato both feel soft and squishy, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? mushy fruit has become extremely soft and easy to squash.

quests.instruction: A green apple and a fresh gooseberry both have this sharp, tangy bite. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This is the taste that's the opposite of a ripe, sugary fruit.
quests.explanation: You found it! A green apple and fresh gooseberry both have this sharp, tangy bite called sour!
quests.funFact: Eating sour candy mimics the taste of very sour fruit.

quests.instruction: Ripe plums and papayas both share this sugary, dessert-like flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste is why so many fruits are eaten as a treat on their own.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! Ripe plums and papayas both share this sugary, dessert-like flavor, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Pineapples and mangoes are incredibly sweet when they are fully ripe.

quests.instruction: A slice of grapefruit and an unripe mango share this same sharp flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This is the taste that makes a fresh lemon so hard to eat plain.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! A slice of grapefruit and unripe mango share this same sharp flavor called sour!
quests.funFact: Did you know? sour fruits have a high level of acidity that makes your mouth pucker.

quests.instruction: A ripe kumquat and a fresh clementine share this bright, zesty flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This taste has a fun zing that wakes up your whole mouth.
quests.explanation: Terrific! A ripe kumquat and fresh clementine share this bright, zesty flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? a tangy flavor is a sharp, strong taste that wakes up your mouth.

quests.instruction: An unripe persimmon and the seeds inside an apple both carry this sharp, unpleasant taste. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste is often a fruit's way of saying it isn't ready yet.
quests.explanation: Yes! An unripe persimmon and an apple's seeds both carry this sharp, unpleasant taste, called bitter!
quests.funFact: Grapefruit has a slightly bitter taste mixed with its sweetness.
